mira (eng-infra): Heads-up — saw repeated latency spikes on us-west2-gpu this morning, correlated with a single tenant suddenly going from steady to bursty qps.
mira (eng-infra): GPU util jumped to 98% for ~3m, preemptible backfills started evicting lower-priority jobs. looked like a short synthetic workload (customer load test).
ops-bot: alert: cluster/us-west2/gpu node_group/gpu-pool-7 high_utilization 2024-05-13T09:12:47Z
dan (sre): Did we route that tenant into a dedicated pool or shared? trying to see why isolation didn't protect others.
mira (eng-infra): It was on shared-pool-3 due to placement rules; tenant had no reserved slice. routing policy picked lowest latency which ended up colocating them with a few latency-sensitive slices.
kevin (runtime): Hmm. if a tenant can burst arbitrarily, shared pools will always risk impacting noisier neighbors. We should limit instantaneous burst by tokenizing burst capacity — a per-tenant "burst credit" that drains while util>threshold and refills slowly.
olivia (product): Curious about UX — would this be visible to customers or purely infra-level? also billing impact? we don't want surprises.
kevin (runtime): infra-level initially. think of a leaky-bucket per tenant: credits used for short bursts (seconds->minutes). once credits exhausted, routing either throttles to baseline or migrates to a higher-cost reserved lane (if purchased).
mira (eng-infra): Implementation idea: track credits in control-plane, expose meter to metrics. policy: when burst_credit<=0, apply soft-ratecap or evict best-effort jobs from that tenant only.
dan (sre): Questions: how do credits interact with Dedicated pools / Reserved slices? should reserved tenants be exempt or use separate quota?
kevin (runtime): Reserved tenants get a separate bucket (much larger refill) — they shouldn't be blocked. For Dedicated, credits are mostly irrelevant; but shared-to-dedicated promotion could be an escape hatch (costly).
olivia (product): If we add a paid escape (promote to reserved for 1h), ops should generate an invoice event. need product spec for billing flows.
mira (eng-infra): quick metric query I ran:
```
sum(rate(gpu_utilization_percent{cluster="us-west2",pool="shared-pool-3"}[1m])) by (tenant)
```
shows tenant A spike ~0.9 at 09:12-09:15.
kevin (runtime): Another routing constraint: we can fail open to model-quantized variants to reduce token compute cost when credits low. e.g., replace 70b fp16 with 13b int8 variant for that tenant's requests.
dan (sre): That helps latency/cost but might affect quality — need product guardrails (A/B or fallback thresholds).
olivia (product): Agree. Add quality-monitoring hook: if fallback reduces eval score > threshold, trigger rollback and notify customer.
mira (eng-infra): Proposed immediate plan:
- prototype burst-credit allocator in canary shared pool (shared-pool-3) (owner: kevin) :rocket:
- metric + alerting: new series tenant_burst_credit{tenant} (owner: mira)
- routing fallback to quantized variant when credit<=20% (owner: kevin + product guardrail by olivia)
- billing escape path design doc (owner: olivia)

kevin (runtime): Will spin up a PoC job next week. timeline: 2w for PoC, 4-6w for safe rollout to one region.
dan (sre): I'll add SLOs/SLIs for eviction count and cross-tenant tail latency so we can measure improvement.
mira (eng-infra): Sounds good. tagging follow-ups: @kevin @olivia @dan. I'll log a short runbook for oncall to temporarily blacklist abusive tenants if needed.
ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-1124 "burst-credit allocator PoC" assigned kevin, due 2024-05-27
olivia (product): Thanks team — product will draft the billing/UX options and quality hooks. will sync after PoC demo. :thumbsup:
mira (eng-infra): closing loop here. if anyone sees the spike again, ping me directly.
